title: The fitted MPI–CNRM radiation-slope contrast lies in shortwave cloud radiative effect in 1980–2014
abstract: We separate fitted radiation responses in seven published AMIP-minus-HighResMIP model pairs into clear-sky and cloud radiative effect (CRE) terms. A common five-model Green function predictor, cubic time control and sea-ice term are fitted to annual means for 1980–2014. The MPI-minus-CNRM-HR net slope contrast is 2.578. SW CRE supplies 2.582; clear sky supplies -0.008. A three-year residual-block interval for SW CRE is 0.531–4.529, but the simultaneous interval over 21 pair contrasts includes zero. A start in 1985 also gives an interval across zero. A control for the 1981 splice retains a positive marginal CRE contrast. Across the seven fitted slopes, CRE supplies 82.5% of covariance-based dispersion, but its interval is -4.9% to 112.5%. The result identifies a radiation component for controlled model tests. It does not identify cloud feedback, assign Green function error to clouds, or establish a universal artifact multiplier. Fixed predictors, short records, experiment differences, model relations and exploratory selection limit inference. Code, aggregate statistics, coefficient draws, source hashes and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: The selected model contrast lies in SW cloud radiative effect at the point estimate. Marginal intervals resolve the CRE terms, but simultaneous intervals over all 21 pair contrasts include zero.

Net, clear-sky and CRE slopes on a common SST radiation predictor. Bars are marginal conditional 95% three-year residual-block intervals. The CRE dispersion share is a descriptive point value with a wide interval.
